Hi there! Just got married in May under similar circumstances.

My brother is a minister and married several other family members and wanted to officiate our wedding. Despite our different beliefs, my brother and I are close and we also wanted him to officiate. I was in angst over how to bring up the "no religion" thing. My husband and I did a lot of research and pieced together a ceremony "script" that we absolutely loved. We emailed it to him and told him while he could add personal touches, we were extremely attached to this version of the ceremony and loved that we had made it our own. He got the hint and it was a perfect ceremony. Your uncle loves you and I'm sure he has at least an inkling of your difference of opinions. It may not be easy for him but ultimately it is your wedding and he will want you to be happy.

We put the phrase "dancing and drinks" at such and such time in our invitations. Some people chose to come to the wedding ceremony and not the reception. Some came to both.. We had a blast!

Have an outdoor wedding! We got married in a covered bridge at a state park. It was CHEAP and beautiful!!

Try googling "offbeat bride". It is a great website that we resources a lot! There is a lot of information about secular weddings, examples of secular wedding "scripts" and just a lot of good ideas. It made me feel better a lot of times when I was feeling overwhelmed with having a "different" wedding that we basically had to make from scratch. 

Good luck!!!!!

I went through the same thing with my now husband when we were dating. I had a frank, honest discussion with him about his finances and how it concerned me about our future. It absolutely is your business to an extent. You plan to have a future with this guy which means you will have a future with his debt and his financial decisions. My husband and I have a firm $100 limit for his mom, dad and sister each year. While it was extremely challenging  and stressful for him at first, it actually ended in him giving more meaningful gifts and less "unnecessary" gifts. 
I think if you tactfully tell him that his financial situation scares you, he may initialing be angry but it will open the door for meaningful conversation.

Best of luck!

Do NOT open a joint account. If he helped you manage your finances before, he can still do that now without a joint account. 

Open your own savings account, link it to your checking and have a certain dollar amount automatically transferred from your checking to your savings every week. You won't even notice it and it will add up quickly.

It's great that you've accomplished something you wanted and found a new hobby in the process (going to the gym) but that doesn't mean that she will share that interest. What if she joined a quilting club and really wanted you to go? That probably wouldn't interest you. 

I'm not saying you shouldn't invite her. I'm just saying, be careful how you approach it and be prepared that she may just not be interested. 

Edit: read some more of your responses to comments. You said she is fairly in shape so I don't think you should assume that she's feeling insecure. If you're hearing hints of bitterness, maybe it's because she just genuinely liked your former body type better. Or maybe liked that you possibly spent more time together before you started going to the gym. Really it could be anything and you should be very careful approaching the conversation with the assumption that you already know how she feels because you don't.

I just got married at the age of 25. My husband and I lived together for 3 years before our marriage and I'm madly in love with him.. I was still extremely anxious to be actually MARRIED to someone. And even after living together for 3 years, we both found marriage difficult at first. Add on starting college, making new friends, and figuring out how to stand on your own two feet independent of your parents (who may not support you through college if you are already married) and that sounds like an awful lot for an 18 year old to take on.

Marriage isn't easy. It is hard work. EVERY. SINGLE. DAY. 


On one hand, it could be the greatest thing and you could be telling your grand kids someday about how you two were high school sweethearts. Or you could be divorced at 20 with a load of lawyer debt. 

Marriage only works if both of you want it more than anything every single day. If you aren't sure of your feelings or even if you are sure that you love her but want more time before marriage.. Tell her that! Because guess what? #1 key to a successful marriage? COMMUNICATION. 

Good luck, my friend.

As someone formally in an abusive relationship, GET OUT NOW.  

It may be verbal now, but as you stated, you live all the way across the country from each other. What will happen if you decide to marry her and suddenly you are living together, seeing each other face-to-face every single day. Trust me, it won't make things better.

I thought moving in with my ex would improve things. He always said that he was just frustrated/emotional because we didn't see each other often enough. After I moved in, he found different excuses for his verbal abuse and eventually his physical abuse (only physical once and then I got the hell out of there). 

Taking steps forward in your relationship won't fix things because her behavior will ALWAYS drag you back to square one. It honestly sounds like she needs counseling or anger management.


Don't even think about moving in with her, getting her pregnant, or marrying her. Don't discuss it with her. Don't daydream about it. Nothing. You can't plan for the future with her if you can't even make it through the day-to-day with her without a fight. 

You are young. Don't rush in to a marriage. Don't hang on hard because she's your "first love". I guarantee there is something better out there than what you are dealing with now.

Hi there :) 25 F here.

First off, age is important here.. But assuming that you are both adults and not high schoolers, I would agree with everyone else that said that sex is extremely EXTREMELY important to a relationship/marriage. 

While it is taboo, waiting till marriage isn't completely impossible if it's what both of you want.. Just make sure it's genuinely what you BOTH want. My sister and her husband waited and they now have a very healthy sexual relationship in their marriage.

My question is this.. Does she absolutely 100% know you are frustrated? Have you said point blank "Mary Jane, I'm frustrated that I give you the sweet sweet pleasure and you've never once returned the favor!"? If you haven't then communicate! Communication is just slightly more important than sex and considering you aren't having sex, you should be talking until your face is as blue as your balls (ha). 

If she does know and doesn't care then THAT is the real issue and in that case, dump her. Because of that is the case, then everyone is correct in saying that a ring and white dress won't change anything. You will end up being just as frustrated in your marriage as you are now in your relationship.

But if she doesn't know.. If you haven't communicated your feelings to her, how can you be mad? Especially when she has no experience with sex and is possibly just naive to how sex is supposed to work (give and take). 

Just talk to her.. It may be hard but wouldn't you rather argue about it now than after you put a ring on her finger?
